Interface ShadedComponentBridge

public interface ShadedComponentBridge
The one entry point that accepts a shaded Adventure component, kept deliberately off NmsBundle.

It lives on its own interface with its own per-module implementation because of how the JVM resolves overrides. NmsBundles loads a module's NmsBundleImpl with Class.forName, and verifying that class checks each override against the interface method it implements, which loads the parameter types. While componentFrom(Component) was declared on NmsBundleImpl, loading any capability from a module dragged the shaded Adventure copy in with it.

That was not theoretical. On a Paper 26.2 server, commandMapModifier dispatches to v1_17_R1; loading that adapter resolved the shaded Component and its six supertypes, on a server that has Adventure natively and touches no shaded text at all. Measured by booting 26.2 with the shaded package deleted from the jar: NoClassDefFoundError ... at NmsBundles.load ... at CommandMapModifierProvider.provide.

Splitting it out means the shaded copy is loaded only when a caller actually asks for a shaded component, which is what VersionedComponentSerializer#fromInternalComponent and VersionedComponent#asInternalComponent exist for. Declaring the type in a method descriptor, as this interface and NmsBundle both still do, does not load it; only an override in a loaded class does.
